types.embedding_query_text: Country: A sovereign state or nation. Also called Nation, State, Realm. Examples: Democratic Republic of Congo, Belgium, UK, Uganda.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'Country' and its mentions perfectly match schema.org/Country.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: SecretaryOfState
candidates.comment: A senior official in the government, typically responsible for foreign affairs.

candidates.label: Archipelago
candidates.comment: A group or chain of islands.

candidates.label: RepresentativeGroup
candidates.comment: A group of individuals acting on behalf of another person or organization.

types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a particular purpose. Also called Institution, Association, Body. Examples: World Health Organization, Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale, Institute of Tropical Medicine, University of Oxford.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'Organization' and its mentions perfectly match schema.org/Organization.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: CharityOrganizationType
candidates.comment: A category of non-profit organization that provides aid or services.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called Individual, Human, Man, Woman. Examples: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Dr Samuel Roger Kamba, pregnant woman, individual.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'Person' and its mentions perfectly match schema.org/Person.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: RepresentativeGroup
candidates.comment: A group of individuals acting on behalf of another person or organization.

candidates.label: Student
candidates.comment: A person who is studying at a school or university.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

types.embedding_query_text: DayOfWeek: A specific day within a week. Also called Weekday, Weekend day. Examples: Thursday.

chosen_type.label: DayOfWeek
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'DayOfWeek' and its mention perfectly match schema.org/DayOfWeek.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: TimeOfDay
candidates.comment: A general period within a day.

candidates.label: HolidayWeekend
candidates.comment: A weekend extended by a public holiday.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: HottestDayEvent
candidates.comment: An event marking the occurrence of the hottest day on record or in a specific period.

types.embedding_query_text: VirusSpecies: A specific type or classification of a virus. Also called Viral strain, Virus type. Examples: Bundibugyo virus, Ebola.

chosen_type.label: Taxon
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/Taxon is the best fit for specific virus species like 'Bundibugyo virus' and 'Ebola'.

candidates.label: InfectiousAgentClass
candidates.comment: InfectiousAgentClass is a medical enumeration of classes of agents or pathogens that transmit infectious diseases. Also called pathogen type, disease agent category, microbial class. Examples: 'Bacteria', 'Virus', 'Fungus', 'Parasite'.

candidates.label: InfectiousDisease
candidates.comment: An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection. Examples: influenza, COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis. Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is a broader category for any health problem.

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

candidates.label: USNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United States. Also called US charity type, American non-profit category, US voluntary sector classification. Examples: a 501(c)(3) organization, a public charity, a private foundation.

candidates.label: RsvpResponseType
candidates.comment: An enumeration type representing the possible responses to an RSVP request. Also called RSVP status, attendance response, invitation reply type. Examples: RsvpResponseType.Yes, RsvpResponseType.No, RsvpResponseType.MayBe.

types.embedding_query_text: City: A large and densely populated urban area. Also called Metropolis, Town, Urban center. Examples: Geneva, Kisangani, Kinshsasa, Ceuta.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'City' and its mentions perfectly match schema.org/City.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: Archipelago
candidates.comment: A group or chain of islands.

candidates.label: Mayor
candidates.comment: The elected head of a city, town, or other municipality.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: Zoo
candidates.comment: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.

types.embedding_query_text: Month: A unit of time, typically one twelfth of a year. Also called Calendar month. Examples: May.

chosen_type.label: Month
chosen_type.definition: A unit of time, typically one of the twelve divisions of the year.
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'Month' and its mention perfectly match vocab/Month.

candidates.label: Month
candidates.comment: A unit of time, typically one of the twelve divisions of the year.

candidates.label: Year
candidates.comment: A period of 365 or 366 days, divided into 12 months, starting from January 1st.

candidates.label: TimeOfDay
candidates.comment: A general period within a day.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific point in time, usually a day, month, and year. Also called Calendar date, Day. Examples: 1 July, Earlier this week, last week, 03/07/2026.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'Date' and its mentions perfectly match schema.org/Date as a specific calendar date.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: TimeOfDay
candidates.comment: A general period within a day.

candidates.label: DateRange
candidates.comment: A specified period of time between two dates.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: HolidayWeekend
candidates.comment: A weekend extended by a public holiday.

types.embedding_query_text: Province: A principal administrative division of certain countries or empires. Also called Region, State, Territory. Examples: South Kivu, North Kivu, Ituri, Tshopo province.

chosen_type.label: State
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/State explicitly includes 'province' in its definition, making it a perfect fit for the OIE_TYPE 'Province'.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: Archipelago
candidates.comment: A group or chain of islands.

types.embedding_query_text: NewsAgency: An organization that gathers news reports and sells them to subscribing newspapers, periodicals, and broadcasters. Also called Press agency, Wire service. Examples: Reuters, AFP.

chosen_type.label: NewsMediaOrganization
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/NewsMediaOrganization explicitly includes 'news agency' in its definition and fits the mentions.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: MediaMonitoringEvent
candidates.comment: An event where media outlets observe and report on a situation.

candidates.label: MediaCoverageEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving media organizations reporting on or observing a situation.

candidates.label: TravelAgency
candidates.comment: A local business that assists individuals and groups in planning and booking travel arrangements. Also called travel agent, tour operator, booking agency. Examples: Expedia, a local independent travel agency, a corporate travel management company.

candidates.label: InsuranceAgency
candidates.comment: An InsuranceAgency is a financial service local business that provides insurance-related services. Also called insurance broker, insurance provider, insurance firm. Examples: State Farm, Geico, a local independent insurance agent.

types.embedding_query_text: Quantity: A measurable amount or number. Also called Amount, Number, Value. Examples: 1.5 million people, four laboratories, 10, six.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'Quantity' and its mentions perfectly match schema.org/Quantity.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: Temperature
candidates.comment: A measure of the warmth or coldness of an object or substance.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

types.embedding_query_text: Duration: The length of time that something continues or exists. Also called Period, Time span, Interval. Examples: two to 21 days, two months.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: The OIE_TYPE 'Duration' and its mentions perfectly match schema.org/Duration.

candidates.label: Duration

candidates.label: TimeOfDay
candidates.comment: A general period within a day.

candidates.label: Year
candidates.comment: A period of 365 or 366 days, divided into 12 months, starting from January 1st.

candidates.label: DateRange

types.embedding_query_text: Disease: A disorder of structure or function in a human, animal, or plant, especially one that produces specific symptoms or that affects a specific location and is not simply a direct result of physical injury. Also called Illness, Sickness, Ailment. Examples: Ebola.

chosen_type.label: MedicalCondition
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/MedicalCondition is the most general and direct fit for the OIE_TYPE 'Disease', as it includes diseases.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: InfectiousDisease
candidates.comment: An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection. Examples: influenza, COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis. Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is a broader category for any health problem.

candidates.label: Substance
candidates.comment: Any matter of defined composition with discrete existence, which can be biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, chemical compound, element, matter. Examples: water, oxygen, penicillin, granite.

candidates.label: Drug
candidates.comment: A Drug is a Product that is a chemical or biological substance used as a medical therapy, having a physiological effect on an organism. Also called medicine, pharmaceutical, medication. Examples: Aspirin, Insulin, Penicillin, Ibuprofen.

candidates.label: Disaster
candidates.comment: A sudden event, such as an accident or a natural catastrophe, that causes great damage or loss of life.

types.embedding_query_text: DiseaseOutbreak: A sudden increase in occurrences of a disease in a particular time and place. Also called Epidemic, Infection surge, Disease flare-up. Examples: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, current deadly Ebola outbreak, current outbreak of Ebola in DR Congo, the outbreak.

chosen_type.label: DiseaseOutbreakEvent
chosen_type.definition: A sudden increase in occurrences of a disease in a particular time and place.
chosen_type.justification: No existing candidate accurately represents a 'DiseaseOutbreak', so a new type is minted as an event and a type of disaster.

mentions: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo

candidates.label: Heatwave
candidates.comment: A period of unusually hot weather.

candidates.label: IncreasedHeatwavesEvent
candidates.comment: An event indicating an increase in the frequency or intensity of heatwaves.

candidates.label: IntenseWildfiresEvent
candidates.comment: An event characterized by wildfires of increased intensity.

candidates.label: FlamesSpreadEvent
candidates.comment: An event where flames expand across an area, typically in a fire.

candidates.label: AlertIssuedEvent
candidates.comment: An event where an alert is officially issued.

types.embedding_query_text: ClinicalTrial: A research study conducted to evaluate a medical, surgical, or behavioral intervention. Also called Medical trial, Drug trial, Research study. Examples: Ebola treatments trial, trial of potential treatments, current trial.

chosen_type.label: MedicalTrial
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/MedicalTrial explicitly includes 'clinical trial' in its definition and fits the mention.

candidates.label: MedicalTrial
candidates.comment: A medical study that uses a scientific process to compare the safety and efficacy of medical therapies or procedures, typically with random allocation to groups. Also called clinical trial, randomized controlled trial, interventional study. Examples: a Phase 3 drug trial, a study comparing two surgical techniques, a vaccine efficacy trial. Distinct from MedicalObservationalStudy, where treatment assignment is not controlled by the investigator.

candidates.label: MedicalObservationalStudy
candidates.comment: A medical study that infers the effect of a treatment by observing a cohort of subjects over time, without investigator control over treatment assignment. Also called observational research, cohort study, epidemiological study. Examples: a study tracking health outcomes in smokers vs. non-smokers, a study on diet and disease incidence. Distinct from MedicalTrial, where subjects are randomly assigned to treatment groups.

candidates.label: MedicalTrialDesign
candidates.comment: An enumeration of design models for medical trials. Also called clinical trial design, trial methodology, study architecture. Examples: "RandomizedControlledTrial", "SingleBlindTrial", "DoubleBlindTrial", "CrossoverTrial".

candidates.label: TherapeuticProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical procedure specifically intended to treat a health condition or improve a patient's well-being. Also called medical treatment, therapy, healing procedure. Examples: chemotherapy, physical therapy, surgical removal of a tumor.

candidates.label: MedicalTherapy
candidates.comment: A therapeutic medical procedure designed to prevent, treat, and cure human diseases and medical conditions. Also called medical treatment, healthcare intervention, therapy regimen. Examples: "pharmacotherapy", "behavioral therapy", "supportive therapy", "dialysis". Distinct from MedicalProcedure, which is a broader category including diagnostic procedures.
